newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures could hold firm soon.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures could hold firm soon.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures could hold firm but inside ranges at least until Thursday's June U.S. employment data, analysts said.
The 111-02/32 to 111-00 area "probably forms a comfortable floor" until the jobs data, Jim Collins, senior vice president, Smith Barney, told Reuters Financial Television.
Economists on average expect nonfarm payrolls to rise 222,000, with a steady, 4.8-percent jobless rate.
Collins would buy at slightly lower levels but said the "upside is somewhat limited" to the June 20 high at 112-24/32 or possibly 113-00 even if payrolls rise only 150,000.
"I don't think momentum is going to be strong enough on the upside to take us significantly above 113-00," he added.

Joel Marver, debt futures technician, Technical Data, said he thought September T-bond futures were "in better shape" than some other forecasters figured and noted that his monthly momentum indicators now point to higher prices again soon.
"With the close of June, we ushered in the first bullish monthly signal since October '96," he said. "It's very rare you don't get higher prices from a turn higher" in the monthly study.
But he said September T-bonds must return above the 111-31/32 to 112-04/32 area to work much higher.
"To get above that would be a sign we could head for new (year's) highs," Marver said. The contract's peak thus far this year was 113-09/23, hit February 18.

Collins also said he doubted September bonds would erode much below 110-28/32 and said a pullback to 110-23/32, Monday's trough, would represent more downside than he expects heading into Thursday's jobs statistics.
Marver pegged the first significant support at 110-20/32, a pivotal area that he said could determine whether prices are able to work upward again and fulfill his forecast, or go lower instead.
"I just wouldn't want to see it break (110-20/32)," Marver said. ((Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
